config.title: Free vs Paid Walking Tour in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: What a free and a paid walking tour in Berlin really cost, how big the groups are and which one suits you.

items.q: Is a free walking tour in Berlin really free?
items.a: It is free to join, and you pay what you decide at the end. **Berlin operators say most guests give between €10 and €50 per person,** and one asks for an optional €3 to confirm a booking. If the guide was poor, you can give less.

items.q: How much does a paid walking tour in Berlin cost?
items.a: Standard public tours from the established operators cost **about €20 to €28 per adult** for two to three and a half hours. Tours with a stated cap of 8 to 15 people range from about €21 to €130 per person. My own walk, Berlin Then and Now, costs €25 per person.

items.q: How big are walking tour groups in Berlin?
items.a: SANDEMANs says it works towards an average of 26 people and tries to stay under 30. Standard paid tours state maximums of 20, 25 or 30. **Tours that put a small number in writing cap at 8 to 15 people.**

items.q: Is a small group walking tour in Berlin worth the money?
items.a: It is if you ask questions, travel with parents or children, or hear less well in street noise. **In a group of 10 nobody stands further than about 2.4 m from the guide.** If your budget is tight or you only want the famous first-day route, a tip-based tour is the better choice.

items.q: What do I get on Berlin Then and Now?
items.a: A walk of about 2.5 hours and about 3 km from the World Clock on Alexanderplatz to Hackescher Markt, with **11 stops covering 16 places and an archive photo of the same place at every stop.** It starts at 12:30 on selected days, costs €25 per person and takes no more than 10 people.

items.q: What happens if I am the only person booked on Berlin Then and Now?
items.a: A walk needs at least 2 guests. **If you are the only guest one hour before the start, I cancel the walk, refund you in full and give you one of my audio walks for free.** Cancellation or a date change is free up to 24 hours before the start.

items.q: Does Berlin Then and Now go to the Brandenburg Gate or the Berlin Wall?
items.a: No. **It stays in the historic centre between Alexanderplatz and Hackescher Markt** and does not go to the Brandenburg Gate, the Reichstag or Checkpoint Charlie. If those are your priority for a first day, take a tour that goes there.
